meta.subline: 17 JUL 2026 · 19:30 GST · US BLOCKADE ENFORCED — TANKER DISABLED OFF KHARG · NIGHT 6 OF STRIKES HITS IRANIAN INFRASTRUCTURE · IRAN HITS KUWAIT WATER PLANT, EXPANDS TO SYRIA · BAB EL-MANDEB CONDITIONAL ORDER REPORTED · BRENT ~$84

banner.html: THE WAR HAS SHIFTED TO INFRASTRUCTURE AND ENFORCEMENT. US disables a tanker off Kharg Island — the blockade is now kinetic · Night 6 of US strikes hits bridges, power and rail in southern Iran; Iran hits Kuwait's power-and-water plant · Tehran reportedly pre-authorises a Houthi Bab el-Mandeb closure if its power grid is hit — that condition has now been met

signals.claim: Reported: Tehran has pre-authorised the Houthis to close Bab el-Mandeb if Iranian power infrastructure is struck — a condition now met.
signals.note: One reporting thread, no Iranian/Houthi official word. Trigger satisfied (power hit 16 Jul); no execution seen. Promotes on any UKMTO advisory; drops if the Red Sea stays quiet.

signals.claim: Circulating as breaking: Iran warns the UAE to evacuate Dubai/Abu Dhabi airports + Fujairah/Jebel Ali ‘tonight.’
signals.note: Recirculation of a 14 Mar ports-only warning that produced no attack; the ‘airports’ detail is aggregator synthesis; NCEMA 17 Jul says stable, threats outside borders. No T2 wire carries a fresh version.

wire.title: Iran hits a Kuwaiti power-generation and water-desalination station — 'widespread damage,' per Kuwaiti authorities.
wire.full: Kuwaiti authorities said Friday that one of the country's combined power and desalination stations was struck in an Iranian attack, causing widespread damage. It is the first confirmed hit on GCC civilian critical infrastructure of the war — every previous confirmed strike in the Gulf states has been on or near US military facilities. No casualty figure released at this update.
wire.why: The target class just changed. For a UAE resident this is the single most consequential item of the week: Gulf desalination plants are existential infrastructure — the UAE's water and power grid is in exactly the class Iran has now demonstrated it will strike. The UAE territorial exemption still holds, but the category protecting it just narrowed again.

wire.src: CENTCOM · Al Jazeera · CNN · Iranian officials
wire.title: Sixth consecutive night of US strikes — southern Iran's civilian infrastructure hit: bridges, airports, power facilities, a train station. Iran reports 8 killed, 20 wounded, warns the war 'will spread.'
wire.full: CENTCOM said its latest wave completed 21:40 ET Thursday (05:40 GST). Iranian officials report civilian infrastructure struck — six bridges in Hormozgan province facing the strait, airports, power facilities and a train station — with at least eight killed and twenty wounded overnight; Iranian health officials put the week's toll at 38 killed and 400+ wounded. The strikes also destroyed a maritime control tower at Chabahar port on the Gulf of Oman — a second commercial gate to the strait, alongside the Kharg blockade fire. Tehran's warning that the war 'will spread' is carried alongside the reported Houthi contingency order (see below).
wire.why: Days after Trump threatened Iranian infrastructure, the strikes moved from military enforcement targets to dual-use and civilian infrastructure. That is escalation in kind, not just tempo — and it armed the trigger condition Iran reportedly attached to the Bab el-Mandeb option. Casualty figures are single-sourced to Iranian officials; treat the numbers as claims, the target shift as real.

wire.title: Iran expands the target map to Syria — claims strikes on US forces there and in Bahrain; Qatar, Kuwait and Jordan fend off fresh waves.
wire.full: The IRGC said it targeted US military forces in Bahrain and, for the first time in this cycle, Syria. Sirens and interceptions reported in Bahrain and Kuwait; Jordan again on the target list. Combined with the Kuwait plant strike a day later, Iran's retaliation set is now geographically wider (Syria) and categorically wider (civilian infrastructure) than at any point since February.
wire.why: Iran is answering vertical escalation (deeper US strikes) with horizontal escalation (more geography, more categories). Widening rather than conceding is the signature of the attrition scenario — and each new geography adds a state whose response could open a front Iran does not control.

wire.src: CENTCOM · Stars and Stripes · The Hill · Gulf News
wire.title: First blockade-enforcement strike: US aircraft disable the Curacao-flagged tanker M/T Belma near Kharg Island — Hellfires into the smokestack; two other vessels turned back.
wire.full: The blockade of Iranian ports resumed 14 Jul (16:00 EDT). Within its first 24 hours, CENTCOM says two compliant vessels were redirected and the Belma — which ignored repeated warnings en route to Kharg Island — was disabled by Hellfire missiles fired into its smokestack, a deliberate propulsion kill designed to avoid rupturing cargo tanks. First US enforcement fire on a commercial vessel since the blockade was reinstated.
wire.why: The mirror image of the GFS Galaxy: now BOTH sides disable merchant ships that defy their rules in these waters. Shipping faces two competing enforcement regimes — Iran's 'unapproved route' fire and America's blockade fire — which is why transits keep falling even with US escorts on offer. War-risk pricing has no precedent for a two-sided enforcement gauntlet.

wire.title: Trump drops the 20% Hormuz toll within a day of floating it — but keeps the blockade and the 'Guardian of the Strait' frame.
wire.full: The toll-on-cargo proposal announced 13 Jul was abandoned by 14 Jul as oil rose and shippers balked; the naval blockade of Iranian ports and the US escort regime remain. The episode ran the full trump-deadline-cycle pattern in ~24 hours: maximal announcement, quiet walk-back, operational policy (blockade + escorts) unchanged throughout.
wire.why: Cleanest read yet on which US moves are real: the toll was rhetoric, the blockade is policy. For the toll-free-window countdown (T−31) this cuts both ways — the US toll is gone, but the MOU's own toll regime is academic while both sides accuse each other of violating the memorandum outright.

wire.src: Israeli officials via ToI/Haaretz — no T2 force movement
wire.title: Israel still out — and Iran is actively working to keep it out, per Israeli assessments; the two re-entry trip-wires stand.
wire.full: Ten days into the exchange, Israeli officials maintain the two-condition frame: Israel rejoins only on a direct Iranian attack on Israel or a US request. Israeli assessments say Iran is deliberately avoiding drawing the IDF in — while Jerusalem cautions the assessment is not certain and prepares for resumed attacks. Herzog: 'you cannot make deals with them.' No T2-confirmed Israeli force movement.
wire.why: The longer Iran sustains targeting discipline that spares Israel while hitting five-plus other states, the clearer it becomes that Israeli entry requires an Iranian decision or mistake — not escalation momentum alone. The tail scenario now hinges on Iranian discipline holding under night-after-night infrastructure losses.

status.v: Six consecutive nights of US strikes. Target set expanded from enforcement (radar, boats, USVs) to infrastructure — six Hormozgan bridges, airports, power, rail, and a Chabahar port control tower. 8 killed/20 wounded overnight; 38 killed and 400+ wounded over the week (Iranian health officials). Blockade of Iranian ports is kinetic: M/T Belma disabled off Kharg 15 Jul.

Widened in geography and kind: claimed strikes on US forces in Syria (first) and Bahrain; Qatar, Kuwait, Jordan under repeated fire; Kuwait power-and-desalination station hit with 'widespread damage' — the first GCC civilian-infrastructure strike. UAE territory still untouched (day 10).

No formal channel since Muscat collapsed 13 Jul. Vance calls the MOU trajectory 'right… just really messy' (podcast, not table); White House principals met 15 Jul; Trump weighing harder options 'in coming days.' Both sides accuse the other of violating the MOU.

US blockade of Iranian ports since 14 Jul, enforced by fire; transits fell 13 → 7/day after it began. Brent ~$84, +10% on the week. Iran's mined-route claim remains uncorroborated — no UKMTO mine advisory; the fast-signal item expired on schedule.

rows.n: A single reporting thread; no Iranian or Houthi official confirmation, no T2 corroboration. Exactly the class of claim the fast-signal ladder holds at pending.

rows.c: The stated trigger condition has been met.
rows.n: US strikes hit power facilities in southern Iran on night six — multiple outlets, Iranian official statements. Whatever the order's reality, its condition is satisfied.

No Houthi attack, UKMTO advisory, or Red Sea traffic shift as of this update. Either the order doesn't exist, or it awaits a decision. The gap between met-condition and non-execution is itself information — watch AIS, not statements.

rows.c: Iranian civilian infrastructure has been hit.
rows.n: Iranian officials detail bridges, airports, power and rail; the US does not deny the target set, framing it as blockade protection. Casualty figures (8 killed, 20 wounded) remain single-sourced to Iranian officials.
Kuwaiti authorities confirmed the hit and 'widespread damage' — the first GCC civilian-infrastructure strike of the war, and the reason the class matters to every Gulf resident.

The US says it strikes blockade-relevant targets; Iran has not formally claimed the plant. Deliberate-targeting intent is asserted by each side about the other and proven by neither. No independent BDA.

verify.quote: The IRGC said the two tankers it struck on 13 Jul had attempted to pass through a 'mined route.'

rows.n: Four days on: no UKMTO mine advisory, no BIMCO warning, no mine incident. The fast-signal item logged 13 Jul reached its TTL without corroboration and is recorded EXPIRED — the listener lifecycle working as designed.

rows.c: Transit behaviour argues against wide-area mining.
rows.n: 7-13 vessels/day have crossed since the claim, plus US-escorted convoys, without a single mine strike. Consistent with no mining or very limited/targeted mining; inconsistent with a mined-shut strait.

market.txt: Brent traded above $84 Friday — on track for a weekly gain of more than 10%, after swinging around $85 Thursday at one-month highs. Transits through Hormuz fell from 13 (Tue) to 7 (Wed), the first full day of the reinstated blockade, and AIS-dark transits mean even those counts are floors, not truth. The Belma strike prices in a new risk: enforcement fire from BOTH sides. The market is now pricing a two-chokepoint scenario tail — any Bab el-Mandeb move would hit Red Sea/Suez routing that the around-Africa alternative cannot fully absorb.

scenarios.lab: Attrition deepens — nightly strikes, kinetic blockade, no talks, strait stays contested
scenarios.p: The modal outcome, upgraded from 45%. Six straight strike nights, a blockade enforced by fire, retaliation widening to Syria and Kuwaiti infrastructure, and a diplomatic track that exists only on podcasts. Nothing in the last 96 hours points to resolution; everything points to grind. Falsifier: a formal negotiation venue is announced, or strike tempo drops for 48+ hours. Analytical judgment, not sourced fact.

scenarios.lab: Horizontal spread — Bab el-Mandeb executes, more GCC infrastructure hit, or Israel is drawn in
scenarios.p: Raised from 25% and now the live tail: the reported Houthi conditional order has a satisfied trigger; Kuwait's plant proved GCC utilities are in the target set; and Israeli entry needs only one Iranian mistake amid nightly infrastructure losses. Any one of the three converts a one-chokepoint crisis into a regional-systems crisis. Falsifier: Red Sea traffic unaffected for 72h AND no further infrastructure strikes on either side.

scenarios.lab: Exhaustion off-ramp — the Vance channel converts to a table and tempo drops
scenarios.p: Downgraded from 30%. The mechanism survives — Vance insists the MOU trajectory is 'right… just really messy,' principals met 15 Jul, and the toll walk-back shows the US still prunes its own escalation. But four days without a single formal session, against six strike nights, is a track record. This scenario now requires both capitals to prefer a messy deal to a grinding win neither can define. Falsifier: a week passes with no venue announced.

uae_means: Day 140 and the UAE territorial exemption still holds — ten days, six strike rounds, and Iran has hit Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, Qatar, Oman and now Syria while leaving UAE soil untouched; the 12 Jul missile alert ended in interceptions before anything entered UAE airspace, and flights are running near-normally (DXB: ~1% cancellations). But the two developments of this cycle both narrow what the exemption protects. First, Kuwait's power-and-desalination station was hit with widespread damage — Gulf desalination is existential infrastructure, the UAE grid is in exactly that class, and the category 'things Iran will strike in the GCC' now includes it. Second, the war acquired a second potential chokepoint: if the reported Houthi Bab el-Mandeb order executes (its trigger condition — US strikes on Iranian power infrastructure — has been met), Red Sea routing gets hit too, and import costs that currently flow around the crisis would be squeezed from two sides. Brent at $84 (+10% on the week) is already feeding fuel and shipping costs. Two UAE-official signals this cycle: Abu Dhabi condemned the strikes on Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan (GCC-solidarity language, not a self-defence shift — the exemption posture holds), and Dubai authorities publicly rebutted false 'explosion in Downtown Dubai' reports and warned they would act against those spreading them — the information war has reached the local layer, so verify before reacting to viral claims. Practical posture: no change to daily life or travel; watch NCEMA/UAE MOD language for any shift from solidarity to self-defence, treat the Kuwait plant strike as the template for the risk that matters locally, and watch Red Sea AIS — not statements — for the Bab el-Mandeb tail. Severe, widening, still territorially contained for the UAE — but the war is now aimed at the systems Gulf life runs on, not just the bases.

triggers.t: Any Houthi move on Bab el-Mandeb — UKMTO advisories and Red Sea AIS, not statements. The reported order's trigger condition is already met; execution converts one chokepoint into two.
A second GCC infrastructure strike — Kuwait's plant made utilities a demonstrated target class. Another (especially water/power in a second state) confirms a deliberate campaign, not a one-off.
Israel's two trip-wires — a direct Iranian attack on Israel or a US request. Iran is visibly working to avoid both; a stray hit on Israeli-linked assets is the mistake that matters.

A formal negotiation venue reappearing — the Vance channel converting from podcast assurances to a table with a date is the only real de-escalation signal. Its absence past ~24 Jul kills the base case.

Enforcement tempo on both sides — Belma-class US strikes on blockade runners and Iranian 'unapproved route' fire. Falling transit counts with rising enforcement fire = the attrition scenario locking in.

hist: War began 28 Feb 2026 — Ali Khamenei killed; Mojtaba Khamenei became Supreme Leader; Iran fired 1,800+ projectiles at the UAE alone (13 killed, 224 injured). MOU signed 17 Jun ('Islamabad Memorandum'): 14 points, 60-day toll-free Hormuz, $300bn reconstruction. 7-11 Jul: tankers struck, three US strike rounds, GFS Galaxy disabled, IRGC declared the strait CLOSED. 12 Jul: Muscat channel opened — two-corridor formula on the table. 13 Jul (Round 4): 140 targets, first sea-drone strikes; Iran hit five GCC states incl. mediator Oman (Duqm); Iranian missiles killed a crew member on the UAE tanker Mombasa; Muscat talks collapsed; Trump declared the US 'Guardian of the Strait.' 14 Jul: the 20% toll floated and dropped within a day; naval blockade of Iranian ports reinstated. 15 Jul: first enforcement strike — M/T Belma disabled off Kharg; transits fell 13 → 7. 16 Jul: sixth strike night hit bridges, power and rail in southern Iran (8 killed per Iran); Iran expanded to Syria; the Houthi Bab el-Mandeb conditional order reported. 17 Jul (Day 140): Iran struck Kuwait's power-and-desalination plant — the first GCC civilian-infrastructure hit; Brent ~$84, +10% on the week. The war is no longer about reopening a strait; it is two enforcement regimes grinding against each other's infrastructure.
